newsitem.title: USA: Court reverses dismissal of LSI Logic suit.
newsitem.headline: Court reverses dismissal of LSI Logic suit.

text.p: A shareholder lawsuit to block LSI Logic Corp from acquiring the public minority interest in LSI Canada has been reinstated by the Delaware Supreme Court, according to court papers.

Shareholder Ethel Taylor of Toronto sued California-based LSI in 1995 to stop it from cashing out through a reverse stock split the 1.7 million shares of LSI Canada not tendered to LSI's Sept 1995 offering of $4 (Canadian) a share.
At issue are differing appraisals of LSI Canada stock at the time of the offer.
The independent banking firm ScotiaMcLeod said the shares were worth C$4.90 to $5.70, but LSI Logic relied on the valuation range of C$2.99 to $3.37 given by its underwriter, Prudential Securities.
The Supreme Court ruling reverses a June 1996 Chancery Court decision to dismiss Taylor's case because Canada would be a "more appropriate forum."

In its decision to reverse, the Delaware high court said the practice in Delaware is to allow plaintiffs their choice of forum and that LSI Logic had no evidence to support its claim that Delaware was an "inconvenient forum."

The court said it also considered the more restrictive discovery rules in Canada and the application there of the English "loser pays" rule. In her lawsuit, Taylor said that rule is "the single greatest obstacle to the prosecution of stockholder class actions in Canada."
